title: Conversion
definition: Conversion is the turning of a sinner from sin to God through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ.
summary: Conversion is the God-given turning of a person from sin to Christ in repentance and faith.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lord to whom sinners turn for mercy, forgiveness, and new life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conversion is the turning of a sinner to God through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. Scripture describes it as a real change of direction, not merely adopting Christian language or improving behavior.

In conversion, a person turns from sin, idols, self-rule, and false hope, and turns to Christ for mercy, forgiveness, and new life. This turning is personal, but it is produced by God's grace through the truth of the Gospel.

Conversion leads to visible change because Christ does not leave people where He found them. The Savior who receives sinners also begins to reorder their loves, loyalties, and steps.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Conversion matters because many confuse religious interest, church attendance, or emotional moments with turning to Christ. This doctrine clarifies that saving faith includes a real turning of the whole person toward God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not rest in vague spirituality or past religious activity. Examine whether you are turning from sin and trusting Christ, and help others understand that coming to Jesus means receiving Him as Savior and following Him as Lord.
